bull: L13 Pairs reversion earns the full 25%: lowest volatility in the book (0.10% a day), a positive unflattered backtest and a small gain through a week in which SPY lost 8.6%. L11 SPY overnight, L12 Turn of month and L9 Sector rotation have the three best unflattered backtest averages (+0.055, +0.073, +0.050% a day), yet the formula gives L11 and L9 nothing; they deserve a share. L5 RSI(2) pullback is the one sleeve built to buy after a week like this one and its backtest is not negative. L16 SPY trend short is the only sleeve that has paid in this regime (+8.8% in five days, positive over 20 and 60 days) and is the natural offset to the long sleeves.
bear: Five live days in a single one-directional selloff say almost nothing: L16, L14 and L15 look brilliant and L6, L8, L9 terrible for the same reason, and a sharp rebound from VIX 36 would flip all of it. L16's backtest average is negative, so its live gain is regime luck, not an edge. The formula's 25% in L10 rests on a flattered, negative backtest and a sleeve that did not trade at all this week, and its 25% in L17 backs a sleeve that has lost over 5, 20 and 60 days; low volatility is not the same as an edge. L1's low volatility also hides a negative backtest. Even the positive backtest averages are a few hundredths of a percent a day over 120 days, well within noise.
risk: Regime is down-stress (five of the last ten days, VIX 35.9). Long-beta sleeves (L11, L9, L5, partly L12) total about 0.38 and fall together on another leg down; L16 at 0.12 offsets part of that, and L13, L10, L17, L1 are low-volatility or often idle. A bad week is a violent bear-market rally intraday that reverses overnight: L16 loses while L11 and L5 also lose, costing perhaps 1.5 to 2.5% on the book. No sleeve is above 25%, none of the breaker sleeves is held, and no short-premium option sleeve is eligible.
decision: Own mix, between risk parity and the formula: L13 0.25, L11 0.12, L12 0.12, L16 0.12, L10 0.10, L5 0.08, L17 0.08, L1 0.07, L9 0.06. Main reason: with five noisy live days and a caution that every simple rule beat the formula on past data, I spread the book over nine sleeves, tilt toward low volatility and non-negative unflattered backtests, halve or more the formula's concentrated bets on L10 and L17, hold nothing in breaker, and keep the book close to market-neutral rather than betting on either continuation or rebound.
